cohort: The study participants were 15,357 women in Indonesia who delivered within the five years prior to the 2017 survey.
finding: Women with secondary education were 2.174 times and those with higher education were 3.241 times more likely to deliver by CS compared to women with no-school education, after adjusting for other factors.
mod_finding: Higher maternal education levels were significantly associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean section delivery in Indonesia.
cross-section timing: Data from the 2017 Indonesia Demographic and Health Survey, including births from the preceding five years (2012-2017).
